title: Optimal Allocation of Design Precision and Verification Effort in AI Assisted Engineering
content: Engineering precision and verification address different uncertainties: precision reduces physical variability, while verification provides evidence that the model predicting performance is valid. In AI assisted engineering, shared modeling errors can propagate through designs and checking procedures, limiting the value of repeated review. This paper develops a framework for jointly allocating component precision and verification effort under an explicit release-risk ceiling. A physical failure certificate combines Gaussian error propagation with a bounded nonlinear remainder and an operating-domain allowance. A Bayesian layer accounts for residual model-invalidating defects, including shared-source errors. Together, these layers establish a release criterion linking physical tolerances to verification requirements. Under exponential detection-response assumptions, minimum-cost verification is a convex optimization problem with an explicit allocation rule. A sensitivity relation shows that marginal verification cost diverges as the physical failure bound approaches the release ceiling. Extensions address uncertain parameters, false rejection, and selective revalidation following configuration changes. A two-link manipulator example demonstrates how certificate conservatism, verification costs, and evidence coverage affect hardware selection and effort allocation. The results provide a tractable method for balancing precision and model assurance. Practical application requires justified physical assumptions, calibrated verification responses, and controlled evidence applicability; no empirical improvement in AI productivity is claimed.
